hook_text: Why does a guitar stay in tune when you let go of the peg? A screw that a wheel cannot turn back.
clip_script: The worm is a shaft with a screw thread. The worm wheel's teeth sit in that thread, shafts at right angles. One turn of the worm, one tooth of the wheel. So a 40-tooth wheel gives 40 to 1 in a single tiny pair: forty turns in, one slow strong turn out. Now push the wheel the other way. Nothing. The thread is too shallow; friction wins. The load stays put. Guitar pegs, winches, gate motors, window winders. The price: a lot of turning, and up to half the energy lost to friction. Slow, strong, and stays put.
visual_style: Whiteboard toothed circle with a threaded cylinder across its top; a counter going 1 to 40 as the wheel ticks round once; a push on the wheel with a red cross; guitar head, winch, gate motor in quick cuts.
mood: Calm and satisfying, like tuning a string.
pacing: Peg, thread and teeth, one tooth per turn, 40 to 1, push back fails, uses, the price.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and count how many peg turns it takes to turn a guitar string post once.
